text: Joints in carpentry are the connections between pieces of wood and are essential for forming strong and stable structures. There are several types of joints, including miter, square, and butt, each serving a different purpose in woodworking. Miter joints, for instance, provide a perfect right angle, ideal for projects requiring precise angles. Carpentry also involves the application of varnish, a protective finish that enhances the appearance and durability of the work. After finishing the carpentry project, applying a varnish ensures the wood remains protected from moisture and wear, prolonging its lifespan and ensuring a smooth final finish.
